retired_before_scoring.reason: The revised p-converse source removes the earlier conductor restrictions for non-CM curves; the global rank-one converse is not an open target.
The p-part at multiplicative primes p>3 with irreducible E[p] is established.
Substantial Eisenstein branches are theorem terrain; a remaining target must name an exact uncovered branch and hypotheses.

candidates.name: 2-primary rank-one leading-term valuation for an ordinary-at-2 semistable class
candidates.statement: For every semistable elliptic curve E/Q of odd conductor, good ordinary reduction at 2, irreducible E[2], and ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=1, prove or disprove the exact ord_2 equality between the normalized complex leading term and the BSD arithmetic quotient.
candidates.rationale: It isolates the prime excluded from the broad p>2 Iwasawa/BSD theorem frontier while retaining a finite-level exact statement and avoiding a claim of full BSD.

candidates.name: 2-primary rank-zero leading-term valuation for the same ordinary-at-2 class
candidates.statement: For every semistable elliptic curve E/Q of odd conductor, good ordinary reduction at 2, irreducible E[2], and L(E,1) nonzero, prove the exact ord_2 equality predicted by BSD.
candidates.rationale: Cleaner than rank one because no regulator is present, but it exercises less of the leading-term architecture and has lower information value for the rank-one frontier.

candidates.name: Soft 2-converse in Selmer corank one
candidates.statement: For a non-CM E/Q with good ordinary reduction at 2 and irreducible E[2], prove that 2-infinity Selmer corank one plus an exact local restriction isomorphism implies complex analytic rank one.
candidates.rationale: A precise p=2 analogue of odd-prime p-converse interfaces, but farther from the exact complex leading-term formula.

candidates.name: Rank-one p-part at an additive reduction prime
candidates.statement: Extend the rank-one p-part formula to a specified additive reduction branch at an odd prime.
candidates.rationale: The additive local branch and correction factors are not normalized tightly enough for theorem-grade selection.

candidates.name: Rank-two derived-height determinant bridge
candidates.statement: Use a rank-two derived or p-adic height determinant to force exact complex and algebraic rank two.
candidates.rationale: Without an independently proved nondegeneracy theorem, the determinant assumption packages the decisive open step.
